blurb: An empty `[]`, `List.empty()`, `Set.empty()` or `Map.empty()` has no elements to take a type from, and the compiler will not guess, because the element type becomes part of the type of everything the collection touches. Give it one: annotate the binding, as `let xs: List[Int] = []`, or use the empty value where a type is expected, such as an argument or a return value. The seed of a `fold` is such a place: `fold(Set.empty(), …)` takes its type from the result the fold is expected to produce, so annotate the result (`let tags: Set[String] = xs.fold(Set.empty(), …)`).
summary: An empty `[]` (or `List.empty()` / `Map.empty()`) has no expected type to infer its element type from.
